# gitmoap_group_sso_invite (Resource)

When the person signs in through the organization's identity provider, they receive the invite's role at the top-level group — a built-in role or one of the organization's own, defaulting to the connection's default role — and the invite is used up. An invite also lets someone without an account in when the connection does not create accounts by itself. Only the organization's owners invite, and an organization holds a limited number of pending invites.

The token needs `sso:manage` and `sso:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String)
- `group_id` (String) The organization's top-level group

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) When the invite stops letting the address in — within a year. Omit it for an invite that
waits until it is used or revoked.
- `reason` (String)

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `expired` (Boolean) Whether that time has passed: the invite admits nobody, and inviting the address again
replaces it.
- `invited_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--invited_by))

<a id="nestedatt--invited_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `invited_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id and email, joined with slashes.
terraform import gitmoap_group_sso_invite.example "<group_id>/<email>"
```
